11. Remote computing

Source: vignettes/articles/guide-remote-computing.Rmd
guide-remote-computing.Rmd

dMod2 parallelizes along two axes: conditions of one objective evaluation in threads, independent fits and profiles in processes. distributedComputing() runs any R code as tasks in processes detached from the session, locally, over ssh or as a SLURM array job. The local job below runs at page build; commands for other machines are shown, not run.

Threads and processes

options(dMod2.cores = n), or obj(pars, cores = n) for one call, solves the conditions of an evaluation in n threads of an OpenMP team inside cppDE, constant in size within a session. The guide model has two conditions, so this axis uses at most two threads; many conditions, or em() with many groups, gain in proportion. A single condition never uses it. Predictions do not pass through forked processes: sending back the arrays of states and sensitivities costs more than computing them.

mstrust(), msem() and profile() run independent fits as processes through cores. With one number, fits are forks of the session, each solving conditions in one thread: a forked child never starts the thread team, and BLAS and OpenMP stay at one thread across the fork. cores = c(fits = 4, conditions = 2) runs four fits with two threads each in fresh R processes (a PSOCK cluster), as always on Windows. Each process holds a copy of the predictions, so memory grows with the process count; keep the product of both below the core count.

where argument axis
one evaluation options(dMod2.cores = ), obj(pars, cores = ) conditions, threads
em() cores groups and conditions, threads
mstrust(), msem() cores, c(fits = , conditions = ) fits, processes
profile() cores, c(pars = , conditions = ) parameters, processes
distributedComputing() tasks, on tasks, detached processes 
options(dMod2.cores = 2)
fits <- mstrust(obj, mu[free], fixed = gauge, sd = sigma[free], fits = 20,
                cores = c(fits = 4, conditions = 2))
profiles <- profile(obj, best, names(best), fixed = gauge, cores = 8)

Tasks and job code

distributedComputing(expr, tasks, on) evaluates expr once per task in a fresh R process; the value is the task result. tasks is a count, a list or vector with one element per task, or a data frame with one row per task. Inside expr:

  • task: the element or row (as a list, task$n), NULL when tasks is a count,
  • taskId: the position in tasks,
  • cores: cores available to the task, e.g. for mstrust(cores = cores), parallel::mclapply(mc.cores = cores) or options(dMod2.cores = cores),
  • jobname: the job name.

input names the session objects the code reads, functions included, by default all objects of the calling environment. The process attaches dMod2 and the R defaults; other packages are loaded by the code, and session options such as dMod2.cores do not reach it.

Example: coverage of the 95% t interval for the mean of exponential samples, one task per sample size, on the local machine:

interval <- function(y) t.test(y)$conf.int
sizes <- data.frame(n = c(5, 10, 20, 50))
job <- distributedComputing(
  {
    message("task ", taskId, ": samples of size ", task$n)
    covered <- replicate(2000, {
      ci <- interval(rexp(task$n))
      ci[1] < 1 && 1 < ci[2]
    })
    data.frame(n = task$n, coverage = mean(covered))
  },
  tasks = sizes, on = localNode(cores = 1), jobname = "coverage", input = "interval", seed = 1
)
#> coverage: 4 tasks started on localhost (1 core)
job
#> Job coverage: 4 tasks on localhost (1 core)
#> check(), wait(), get(combine = TRUE, all = FALSE), log(i), purge(local = FALSE), terminate()

The call returns once tasks have started. job is a list of functions: check() reports task states, wait() polls until none runs, get() joins the results, here into one data frame.

job$check()
#> coverage: 0 of 4 tasks done, 4 running
job$wait(interval = 1)
#> coverage: 0 of 4 tasks done, 4 running
#> coverage: 1 of 4 tasks done, 3 running
#> coverage: 2 of 4 tasks done, 2 running
#> coverage: 3 of 4 tasks done, 1 running
#> coverage: 4 of 4 tasks done
job$get()
#>    n coverage
#> 1  5   0.8760
#> 2 10   0.8960
#> 3 20   0.9285
#> 4 50   0.9445

Task i uses seed seed + i, independent of worker and order; without seed one is drawn. A task that errors returns the try-error, the others go on.

Job folder layout

At submission the job files go into a temporary stage, copied to every node as one tar stream over ssh into <jobname>_folder/<k> of the home directory, k the node number. On "localhost" the folder is in the working directory and no ssh is used. The local <jobname>_folder also holds the manifest job.rds. After the local job:

list.files("coverage_folder", recursive = TRUE)
#>  [1] "1/job.R"           "1/slot_1.pid"      "1/slot_1.sh"      
#>  [4] "1/task_1.out"      "1/task_1.rds"      "1/task_2.out"     
#>  [7] "1/task_2.rds"      "1/task_3.out"      "1/task_3.rds"     
#> [10] "1/task_4.out"      "1/task_4.rds"      "1/tasks.rds"      
#> [13] "1/workspace.RData" "job.rds"
file content
workspace.RData objects of input; zstd-compressed when available locally
tasks.rds tasks as a list, one entry per data frame row
job.R R script of a task
model files sources, objects or shared objects, see Model files and builds
build.sh, files.txt, build.log model build on the node, build output
slot_<k>.sh, .pid, .run runner script of node k, process ID of the script and of the running task
job.sh, env.sh SLURM only: job script from the template, job environment
task_<i>.out, task_<i>.rds output and result of task i

job.R is the same for every task, called as Rscript job.R <taskId> <cores> with output in task_<taskId>.out:

writeLines(readLines("coverage_folder/1/job.R"))
#> library(dMod2)
#> load('workspace.RData')
#> for (so in list.files(pattern = paste0('[.]', substring(.Platform$dynlib.ext, 2L), '$'))) dyn.load(so)
#> taskId <- as.integer(commandArgs(TRUE)[1L])
#> cores <- as.integer(commandArgs(TRUE)[2L])
#> task <- readRDS('tasks.rds')[[taskId]]
#> jobname <- 'coverage'
#> set.seed(1 + taskId)
#> result <- try({
#> {
#>     message("task ", taskId, ": samples of size ", task$n)
#>     covered <- replicate(2000, {
#>         ci <- interval(rexp(task$n))
#>         ci[1] < 1 && 1 < ci[2]
#>     })
#>     data.frame(n = task$n, coverage = mean(covered))
#> }
#> })
#> saveRDS(result, paste0('task_', taskId, '.part'))
#> invisible(file.rename(paste0('task_', taskId, '.part'), paste0('task_', taskId, '.rds')))

It attaches dMod2, loads workspace and shared objects, reads the task, sets the seed and evaluates the code in try(), writing task_<taskId>.rds for get(). Tasks share nothing but files. The code runs in the job folder of the node; files written there come back with get(all = TRUE).

Nodes and workers

on says where tasks run:

on <- localNode()                                        # the local machine, with the free cores
on <- localNode(cores = 8)
on <- sshNodes(c("server1", "server2"))                  # each node with the free cores there
on <- sshNodes(c("server1", "server2"), cores = 10)
on <- sshNodes(cores = c(server1 = 24, server2 = 20))
on <- sshNodes(c("localhost", "server1"))                # the local machine and one more
on <- slurmCluster("mycluster", cores = 8, walltime = "12:00:00")

A node is an ssh destination ("host", "user@host") with key authentication, since no terminal takes a password. "localhost" runs without ssh, in the session shell and working directory, with the R and library paths of the session, so no second dMod2 install is needed; localNode() is sshNodes("localhost").

Each node is one worker. Task i goes to worker (i - 1) %% W + 1 of W; a worker runs the assigned tasks in sequence, each with the cores of the node. tasks = NULL, the default, gives one task per worker.

cores per task is one number, a vector named by node, or NULL for the free cores at submission. detectFreeCores() counts cores minus the one-minute load average, on a local Windows machine minus the processor load since the previous call, at least 1, locally or over ssh; a node gets at most the free cores, with a warning if given more.

detectFreeCores(c("localhost", "server1", "server2"))

On each node slot_<k>.sh calls Rscript job.R for each task of the node in turn, started as nohup setsid sh slot_<k>.sh &, so it survives the end of the ssh connection or the session. Tasks run with OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 and MKL_NUM_THREADS=1, so BLAS and OpenMP start only threads the code asks for, and with libs first in the library paths.

Model files and builds

The model files of a job are those of the model objects in input (obsfn, parfn, prdfn, objectives), found through their sources; without any, all model files of getOption("dMod2.outdir"), else of the working directory. build sets how they reach the nodes:

  • "compile": sources are copied and build.sh compiles them into one shared object against the cppDE installed on the node, with cppDE headers, SUNDIALS, KLU, the model -D switches and -O2. buildCores compilers run at once, by default the node cores, at most 16. Past the command-line limit objects go through a static archive, buildBundle sources per translation unit.
  • "link": object files are copied and linked, which needs a compatible compiler on the node.
  • "copy": shared objects are copied, which needs a compatible node.
  • "auto", the default: "copy" when all nodes are "localhost", else "compile".

The build runs once per node before the first task; job.R points every model object of the workspace at the one shared object (modelname()). On SLURM it runs once on the login node for all array tasks. Output goes to build.log; a failed build stops the submission and shows the end of the log. libs prepends library paths on the nodes for build and tasks, expanded remotely, so ~ is the remote home.

The coverage job has no model files: no model object in input, no shared object in the working directory.

Job monitoring and recovery

function does
check() counts done, running, failed; TRUE once none runs, warns on failures
wait(interval = 10) polls until none runs, reports changes; TRUE if all done
get(combine = TRUE, all = FALSE) returns the results
log(i, lines = 20) last output lines of task i
purge(local = FALSE) deletes the job folders on the nodes, on "localhost" the local <jobname>_folder/<k>, with local = TRUE also local folder and registry entry
terminate() stops the tasks

A task is done when the result file exists, running while the worker runs (also while waiting), failed when the worker ended without a result. get() copies remote results over ssh into the local <jobname>_folder/<k>, with all = TRUE all files. It joins parlists with c() and data frames, parameter frames included, with rbind(), which merges the two sides of a profile; other results come as a list. Missing results are dropped with a warning. get(combine = FALSE) returns one entry per task, named like tasks: NULL if not done, the try-error if failed. terminate() ends the process group of every slot, on SLURM the job by scancel.

Output of the second task, then deletion:

job$log(2)
#> task 2: samples of size 10
job$purge(local = TRUE)

distributedComputing(wait = TRUE) waits, returns get() and deletes the job; a job with failed tasks is kept for log().

A job outlives the session. The manifest is in the local <jobname>_folder, in the <jobname>_folder of every remote node until purge(), and in the registry tools::R_user_dir("dMod2", "data") until purge(local = TRUE); dMod2Jobs() lists registered jobs. recover = TRUE with a job name returns the job functions without resubmitting, from the manifest in the working directory, else the registry, else, with on, the remote node folders, which recovers a job from another machine. A new job of the same name is an error while the old one runs where the new one would replace the old folders: in the same working directory or on the same remote nodes, also from another machine.

dMod2Jobs()
job <- distributedComputing(jobname = "fits", recover = TRUE)
job <- distributedComputing(jobname = "fits", on = sshNodes(c("server1", "server2")),
                            recover = TRUE)

SLURM clusters

slurmCluster() names the login node, reached by ssh, and the resources per array task: cores, walltime, memPerCore in GB. Workers are the array array tasks, by default one per task; array task j runs tasks j, j + array, j + 2 * array, … in sequence. The stage goes to ~/<jobname>_folder/1 on the login node, where the template environment is set up, the model files are built once, and sbatch submits from that folder, so compute nodes must see the login-node home directory. partition, account, maxRunning (array tasks at once) and sbatch (further options such as "--constraint=ib") override the #SBATCH lines of the template. The start reports the job ID; check() reads squeue, terminate() calls scancel.

slurmTemplate() sets up the job script template once per login node, stored in tools::R_user_dir("dMod2", "config"). A template is a cluster job script with placeholders {{ jobname }}, {{ ntasks }} (array tasks), {{ cores }}, {{ memPerCore }}, {{ walltime }}, and one line {{ run }} that runs the tasks. Non-comment lines before {{ run }} set up the environment, e.g. module load, also for the build on the login node. A placeholder without value is an error, so {{ walltime }} needs walltime. The shipped template for the bwForCluster Helix:

writeLines(readLines(system.file("slurm", "helix.sh", package = "dMod2")))
#> #!/bin/bash
#> # Job script template of distributedComputing() on slurmCluster("helix", ...) for
#> # the bwForCluster Helix, set up with slurmTemplate("helix"). The {{ ... }} fields
#> # are filled in, {{ run }} runs the tasks of one array task.
#> #SBATCH --job-name={{ jobname }}
#> #SBATCH --array=1-{{ ntasks }}
#> #SBATCH --partition=cpu-single
#> #SBATCH --nodes=1
#> #SBATCH --ntasks-per-node={{ cores }}
#> #SBATCH --mem-per-cpu={{ memPerCore }}gb
#> #SBATCH --time={{ walltime }}
#> #SBATCH --output=slurm_%A_%a.out
#> 
#> module load compiler/gnu/13.3
#> module load math/R
#> 
#> {{ run }}
slurmTemplate("mycluster", from = "~/mycluster.sh")   # once, from a job script, for editing
slurmTemplate("helix")                                 # the template dMod2 ships for Helix
slurmTemplate()                                        # the templates set up
cluster <- slurmCluster("helix", cores = 1, walltime = "12:00:00")

slurmCluster(jobscript = ) takes another template for one job.

Fits and profiles of the guide project

A cluster starts many small tasks sooner than one large one, so these jobs use one core per task. The 200 fits of fit.R (Optimization) as 200 one-fit tasks, each start drawn from the task seed:

free <- setdiff(names(mu), names(gauge))
fitsJob <- distributedComputing(
  mstrust(obj, mu[free], fixed = gauge, sd = sigma[free], fits = 1, iterlim = 1000, tolControl = tolerances),
  tasks = 200, on = cluster, jobname = "oppelt_fits", seed = 1,
  input = c("obj", "mu", "sigma", "free", "gauge", "tolerances"))
fitsJob$check()
fitsJob$wait(interval = 60)
fits <- as.parframe(fitsJob$get())
fitsJob$purge(local = TRUE)

The sources of obj compile once on the login node. get() joins the parlists, as.parframe() sorts by value. A later session, also on another day, takes up the job by name:

fitsJob <- distributedComputing(jobname = "oppelt_fits", recover = TRUE)

The profiles of Profile likelihood, one side of one parameter per task:

sides <- expand.grid(par = names(best), side = c("left", "right"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
profilesJob <- distributedComputing(
  profile(obj, best, task$par, side = task$side, fixed = gauge,
          limits = c(lower = -7, upper = 7), stepControl = list(stop = "data"),
          algoControl = list(reoptimize = TRUE),
          optControl = list(iterlim = 100, tolControl = tolerances)),
  tasks = sides, on = cluster, jobname = "oppelt_profiles",
  input = c("obj", "best", "gauge", "tolerances"))
profilesJob$wait(interval = 60)
profiles <- profilesJob$get()

get() binds both sides of each parameter into one profile.

An msem() multistart splits by which: every task draws all starts from the same seed and fits those it names. The 200 starts of Sparse deviations, two per task:

compoundsJob <- distributedComputing({
  set.seed(3)
  msem(objCompounds + priorCompounds, random, init, fixed = gaugeReduced, fits = 200,
       sd = sdStart, keepFits = TRUE, which = task)
}, tasks = split(1:200, rep(1:100, each = 2)), on = cluster, jobname = "oppelt_compounds",
input = c("objCompounds", "priorCompounds", "random", "init", "gaugeReduced", "sdStart"))
fitCompounds <- compoundsJob$get()

get() returns one msem() fit, the best, with table and fits of all starts. helix.R of the project runs the other expensive guide scripts the same way.

Without SLURM, as many tasks run at once as there are nodes. One task per node, the default, with ten fits per node core:

fitsJob <- distributedComputing(
  mstrust(obj, mu[free], fixed = gauge, sd = sigma[free], fits = 10 * cores, iterlim = 1000,
          tolControl = tolerances, cores = cores),
  on = sshNodes(c("server1", "server2")), jobname = "oppelt_fits", seed = 1,
  input = c("obj", "mu", "sigma", "free", "gauge", "tolerances"))

Bile acid transport runs the multistarts as a local job, Kok 2020 the 200 fits as a SLURM array job.

System requirements

  • A POSIX shell locally (on Windows the sh of Rtools) and on every remote node, bash on remote nodes for build = "compile" (default) and "link".
  • Remote nodes: ssh with key authentication, dMod2 and cppDE for the R on the node PATH or in libs, a compiler for build = "compile".
  • SLURM: an account on the login node, a template from slurmTemplate(), a home directory visible to the compute nodes.
  • zstd on every remote node if the local machine has it, since it then compresses the workspace.

Reference: distributedComputing(), localNode(), sshNodes(), slurmCluster(), slurmTemplate(), detectFreeCores(), dMod2Jobs(), mstrust(), msem(), profile()
